scope_note: Targeted architecture sweep over public patent metadata and user-supplied USPTO front pages. This is not a complete read of every USPTO PDF or every result in the Palantir query.

research_method.meaning: 100 virtual analysis roles for partitioning research themes and documents; this repository does not claim that 100 independent external agents were executed in this chat.

architecture_signals.signal: Generate ontology definition artifacts and SDKs from governed object-type definitions.
Permission-aware ontology queries can be transformed into database work and routed across execution environments.
A unified ontology API can route requests to different backing object databases.
AI workflow performance can be evaluated over time with developer and operations views.
LLMs can assist root-cause summaries and proposed remediation using prior incident context.
Error logs plus contextual data can be converted into explanation and suggested-fix workflows.
Automation, action, and data objects can be rendered as an interactive dependency graph.
Applications can advertise capabilities and synchronize shared state through governed messaging.
AI-assisted API discovery and configuration can support tool selection and integration workflows.
Generative models can help map unstructured inputs into hierarchical data structures.
Structured user-action logging enables object-level investigations and audit review.
Ontology-backed applications can be built with explicit cache strategies for disconnected operation.
Versioned transform logic can be synchronized across edge servers while normalizing lagging outputs.
Task objects can be linked to data objects and presented with location/context metadata.
Large geospatial/object collections can be clustered and explored interactively.
AI-assisted risk workflows can combine extraction, screening, analysis, scoring, and audit history.
Observed workflows can be converted into auditable documentation with AI assistance.
Criteria can be modeled as linked object types and evaluated with governed modalities and instructions.
Multi-source imagery can be registered before higher-level object correlation; ZYRA-MSS limits this pattern to non-targeting defensive or civilian analytics.
Candidate associations across sensor tracks can be confidence-scored and merged; ZYRA-MSS does not use this for hostile targeting or weapons control.

zyra_mss_design_principles: no weapons release, autonomous targeting, or hostile engagement control
